clue.text: Pay them with change and compassion

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters before this phrase get altered in order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to reward staff both with money and with kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay them with change' reads like handing over coins; the change is a rearrangement of the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the feeling of sharing and understanding another person's suffering, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: French clown's dirty broadcast on the radio

indicators.note: what goes out on the radio is heard rather than seen, so only the sound of the words counts

parts.note: to dirty something is to mar it, and to broadcast seed is to sow it; said together they make 'mar-so'

explanation.surface: A French clown has made an off-colour remark during a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like it belongs with the radio, but it is the farmer's sense of scattering seed; MAR and SOW, said aloud, give the French surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Marceau was the celebrated French mime artist whose white-faced character Bip was a sad clown figure.

clue.text: Politicians were concealing outcome of enquiry

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep something tucked out of sight within, so the letters lie buried inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Politicians covered up what an official inquiry found.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cover-up; the concealing is literal, across the join of the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: What you get when you ask a question is a reply, so the result of a query is its reply or response.

clue.text: Suffer in the wake of hot weather

indicators.note: a wake trails behind a ship, so what comes in its wake is placed after what precedes it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
to ail is to suffer or be unwell

explanation.surface: Someone feels unwell after a spell of hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot weather' reads as one phrase, but 'hot' is only its abbreviation and 'weather' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling pellets of ice are one kind of weather, an example of the general noun for conditions in the sky.

clue.text: Emperor's vehicle circumnavigating westward ocean

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to go right round something, so one piece travels all the way around another

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in an across clue westward means right to left, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: an ocean is a sea

explanation.surface: A ruler's ship sails right round the globe, heading west across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue westward means right to left. The 's after the definition is read as 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became the title of Roman rulers after Julius, so it is a byword for an imperial monarch.

clue.text: Notice posh clubs and racist organisation infiltrating southern city

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get in secretly behind the lines, so these pieces slip inside another

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
U means upper-class, the posh register of English
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
the Klan is the Ku Klux Klan

explanation.surface: Upper-class clubs and a racist group have infiltrated a southern city.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a long-standing British label for posh speech and manners. 'Southern' is about the hemisphere, not the south of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Auckland is the largest city of New Zealand, far down in the southern hemisphere, hence described by its latitude.

clue.text: Partners to capture freewheeling rogue operator

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: in bridge, South and North play as partners

indicators.note: freewheeling means moving loosely without control, so these letters run in a loose new order

parts.note: taken as written, five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Two partners set out to catch a reckless con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, with N and S a partnership; they go around a reshuffle of ROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon operates on patients, so the general term for someone who carries out operations fits.

clue.text: Had another look at fashionable, reputable clothing

indicators.note: clothing covers a body, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: someone reputable is well thought of
what is in is in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone took a second look at clothes that are both stylish and respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like the thing being looked at, but it is the wrapping instruction; 'fashionable' goes inside 'reputable'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, so to do it again is to examine for a second time.

clue.text: Right-wing populist slogan turned angry men against legendary military leader

indicators.note: to turn something round sends it back the way it came, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: MAGA is Make America Great Again, the Trump campaign slogan

indicators.note: someone angry is worked up and agitated, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, three letters to rearrange
leaning on something is leaning against it

explanation.surface: A populist slogan has turned a crowd of angry men against a famous general.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGA backwards, then a shuffle of MEN, then ON. 'Angry men against' reads as the men opposing someone, but 'against' just supplies its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, commanded the Greek armies in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Traversing cold Antarctic sea wearing gilet top

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the Ross Sea is an arm of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica
you are in the clothes you are wearing

indicators.note: the top of a down-written word is its opening, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the garment

explanation.surface: An explorer crosses a freezing polar sea dressed in a sleeveless jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing gilet top' sounds like clothing advice; it gives IN and the first letter of the gilet. A gilet is a sleeveless padded jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to go from one side to the other, the same action as going across.

clue.text: King retaining old soldier, one of the late queen's favourites?

definitions.text: one of the late queen's favourites?

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
O is the abbreviation for old
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The king keeps on an old soldier who was a favourite of his late mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Carolus Rex fits the surface neatly, since King Charles succeeded the late queen; the old soldier splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept Pembroke Welsh corgis all her life; the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: Musk's company drones possibly gathering to pursue current prey in Africa

indicators.note: what pursues something follows behind it, so this group is placed after the other

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: to gather is to collect up and hold, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: drones are male bees, 'possibly' flagging the example
X is Elon Musk's renamed Twitter

explanation.surface: Elon Musk's firm has flying drones massing to chase quarry across Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: BEES gathers X, and that whole follows I. 'Drones' suggests flying machines to go with Musk; here they are male bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubian ibexes live in north-east Africa, where leopards and other predators hunt these wild goats.

clue.text: One Liberal Democrat finally breaking rank

indicators.note: something that breaks falls apart, so these letters are smashed and put together anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the party member

explanation.surface: A single Lib Dem has broken ranks with the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking rank' reads as a political rebellion; the rank is the definition, an adjective, and 'Liberal' must be used whole, not abbreviated to L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means offensive or outrageous, as in rank injustice, something too gross to bear.

clue.text: Those at the coalface with two trainees covering for new people on the daily grind

indicators.note: to cover for a colleague is to stand in for them, so one piece takes another's place

parts.note: coal miners work at the coalface
L for learner, doubled
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Coal workers and two apprentices stand in for new staff on the everyday slog.
explanation.walkthrough: The LL replaces the N in MINERS. L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Millers grind grain into flour, so the 'daily grind', normally an idiom for routine work, is literal for them.

clue.text: Perhaps Wiccans' song gets confused with paean

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A witches' coven's chant gets mixed up with a hymn of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song' and 'paean' look like a pair of synonyms to be swapped; both are used letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is a modern revival of pre-Christian religion, so Wiccans are one example of present-day followers of such faiths.

clue.text: Genuine amateur theatre's somewhat revolutionary

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the run of letters is used
a revolution is a turning round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second, read right to left

explanation.surface: A real amateur theatre company stages fairly radical work.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'amateur theatre' and must be read backwards; 'revolutionary' fits the surface as edgy drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Something genuine is real and authentic, the same sense as a real or faithful article.

clue.text: Immortality for every person in French church

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'
a man is a person
en is French for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Eternal life is promised to everyone in a church in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French church' reads as a location; 'in French' is EN and 'church' is CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortality is lasting for ever, and the noun for that lasting quality is endurance without end.

clue.text: American uncle is reportedly meeting daughter engaged in dissident activity

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: the word is pronounced with a buzzing final sound
D is the abbreviation for daughter
to be at a task is to be engaged in it

explanation.surface: An uncle from the States meets his daughter, who has turned political rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling IZ is the sound of 'is'. 'American uncle' suggests a relative, but it is the national figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Samizdat was the secret copying and circulation of banned writing in the Soviet bloc, a form of underground protest.

clue.text: Tabloid centrally features a review of very therapeutic place for dogs

indicators.note: centrally means at the centre, so only the middle letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters
something that features an item has it
taken as written

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
a spa is a place for healing treatments

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a write-up of a luxury pet spa for dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: SO SPA read backwards gives APSOS. 'A review' looks like a newspaper article; it is 'a' plus the backwards signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa apsos are a small long-haired Tibetan breed, named after Lhasa; the plural answer matches the plural noun.

clue.text: Song describing cut-off area in US state

indicators.note: something cut off has lost its end, so the final letter goes
to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a zone is an area, without its final E

explanation.surface: A song tells of a remote, isolated region of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' reads as telling about; in geometry it means drawing round, so ARIA surrounds the shortened ZONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is one of the fifty United States, in the south-west of the country.

clue.text: Good, slow down to prepare for ice

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
rit. is ritardando, the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Sensible advice to drivers: slow down when there's ice about.
explanation.walkthrough: Rit. is the score marking for ritardando, gradually slower. 'Slow down' reads as driving advice, but it is music.
explanation.definitionFit: Councils spread sand and salt on roads before a frost so that tyres keep traction on icy surfaces.

clue.text: Intend to wear torn clothing

indicators.note: what you wear surrounds you, so one piece is put on inside the other

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, to tear
to aim to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: Someone plans to go out in ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torn clothing' looks like one phrase; 'torn' supplies the outer piece and 'clothing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old, literary word for garments, what a person has on.

clue.text: Society writer's petition short and straightforward

indicators.note: something short is lacking length, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
the setter, the writer, says 'I'm' for 'the writer is'
a plea is a petition, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A society columnist's appeal is brief and to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' reads as possessive; it is 'writer is', with the writer being the setter, so I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncomplicated and easy to follow is plain and without difficulty, close synonyms.

clue.text: Mentioning one transgression covered by tabloid

indicators.note: what is covered by something has it all round, so these pieces sit inside another

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
I is the Roman numeral one
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: Bringing up a single misdeed that a gossip paper has reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered by tabloid' sounds like press coverage; it is the wrapping signal. A rag is slang for a cheap newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a topic is to bring it up in conversation, so the two participles share the sense of introducing a subject.

clue.text: Given 1 or 2 types of mine?

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
an IED, improvised explosive device, is a roadside mine

explanation.surface: A question about whether one or two kinds of mine are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is the answer to 1 Across, EMPATHY. '1 or 2' looks like a count, but 1 is a cross-reference and 2 counts the mines: a dig and a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shown sympathy for one's suffering is being felt sorry for, so given compassion means pitied.

clue.text: Lead beginning of sales pitch

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
pitch is the black sticky substance, tar

explanation.surface: A tip about how to open a sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sales pitch' reads as one phrase; 'pitch' alone is the sticky substance, not the patter.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead in a film or play is its principal performer, whose name tops the bill.

clue.text: Vital fluid in flower ultimately halved

indicators.note: to halve is to cut in two, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: in flower is blooming; the first four of its eight letters

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: The sap inside a flower has finally been reduced by half.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOOMING cut in half leaves BLOO, and the last letter of 'halved' finishes it, so 'halved' works twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood is the fluid the body cannot live without, carrying oxygen round it; vital means essential to life.

clue.text: No short release on cassette — no sound at all

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece placed on another sits after it

parts.note: taken as written
a cassette is a tape
an EP, extended play, is a record release shorter than an album

explanation.surface: A band has put out no short release on cassette, leaving fans with silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short release' suggests an abbreviation or cut; it is an EP, which sits after TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is the smallest sound, so not even that means complete silence, an idiom for utter quiet.

clue.text: Brings about new stance

indicators.note: what is new has been made afresh, so these letters are remade in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something causes a change of position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New stance' reads as a fresh opinion; 'new' is the signal and 'stance' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a law or plan is to put it into effect, so it causes it to happen.

clue.text: Express sadness about European Union returning officer's sadism

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed around the others

parts.note: to cry is to express sadness

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: EU is the European Union
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: Lamenting a Brexit-style officer's taste for inflicting pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning officer' looks like the election official who announces results; here 'returning' turns the Union round and 'officer' is a lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is taking pleasure in hurting others, and the broader noun is a pitiless, callous disposition.
